name: SnapKV (observation-window KV selection) - NOT KV quantization
bits: none - selects important KV POSITIONS per attention head from an observation window; no bits are reduced.
activation_scheme: None. Fine-tuning-free: each attention head is observed to focus on stable prompt-attention features during generation, and this pattern can be read off an 'observation window' at the end of the prompt. SnapKV then selects clustered important KV positions per head.
kernels: Runs in HuggingFace implementations with minor changes, and fits 380K context tokens on a single A100-80GB.
quality_delta: From the abstract: 3.6x increase in generation speed and 8.2x memory-efficiency improvement over baseline at 16K-token inputs, comparable performance across 16 long-sequence datasets, and only a negligible accuracy drop on Needle-in-a-Haystack.
notes: GROUP SIZE NOT APPLICABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: eviction reduces HOW MANY KV positions are retained; no bits per retained value change, so there is no weight grid to group. The null here is a fact about the method, not missing data. Boundary record. SnapKV's fine-tuning-free property is what distinguishes it operationally from learned approaches - it works on any checkpoint with no retraining and no calibration pipeline, which is why it spread into serving stacks faster than most of this literature. Its observation-window trick is the same underlying fact H2O identified (attention concentrates) applied at the prompt level rather than the token level. The 8.2x memory-efficiency figure at 16K tokens is a prompt-length-specific measurement; memory savings from eviction scale with context length, so quoting it outside that regime would be misleading.
